recentItems.title: Activists in Israel protest against settler violence in West Bank | ABC NEWS
recentItems.description:
Peace activists gathered near the Jerusalem home of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu this week, to protest against settler violence in the West Bank.

recentItems.title: Australian expert assists in tunnel rescues following Nepal floods | ABC NEWS
recentItems.description:
Two people have been rescued alive from a hydropower tunnel in Nepal nine days after devastating floods hit the country.

Australian geologist and engineer Arnold Dix has been assisting Nepali authorities from his home in rural Victoria as they scoured the devastated landscape looking for survivors.

Professor Dix said the use of explosives to blow up damaged land and infrastructure to remove it in the hope of finding tunnel entry-ways has never been done before.

He said the Australian government asked him to fly to Nepal in the aftermath of the disaster, but he stayed in Monbulk because he had a solid data connection there that allowed him to connect with rescuers on the ground.

"That meant helping the team identify where the power station used to be, using satellite images coming out of helicopters," he told ABC News Channel.

About 900 workers are missing from 12 hydropower projects in Nepal, with roughly 500 believed to be trapped in tunnels, according to local authorities.

The tunnelling expert is currently in Singapore where he is en route to Nepal to further assist rescue efforts on the ground.

recentItems.title: Australian homes more unaffordable than ever despite property downturn | ABC NEWS
recentItems.description:
Australian housing affordability has hit its lowest point on record despite an ongoing downturn in property prices, according to new data from Realestate.com.au. 
The report shows the median income household could afford only 12 per cent of homes sold in the 2025-2026 financial year due to high house prices and three consecutive rate hikes by the Reserve Bank. 
REA Group’s Angus Moore says the rate rises have so far mainly affected the high-end sector of the property market while the government’s tax reforms are not expected to have a big impact on housing affordability.

recentItems.title: Families go to great lengths to search for missing Australians after Nepal-Tibet floods | ABC NEWS
recentItems.description:
Relatives of Australians missing after the Tibet-Nepal flooding disaster have flown to the area in search of their loved ones. 
Bhavin Patel hired a helicopter to look for his wife Reshma near the border between Tibet and Nepal after he was told she was last seen on the Chinese side of the border. 
Families of missing Australians have welcomed the arrival of an Australian specialist drone team but are also urging Nepalese and Chinese authorities to do more to locate more survivors.
